precepts.text: I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him. That is taking accountability. Until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he shall bring me forth to the light. Why? Because I do not dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging, making excuses, or blaming the brothers for not checking in on me. Take your medicine and move on. I do not judge a person by the infraction so much as by what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk means nothing if you ghost as soon as correction comes.
precepts.point: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways: always tossed around, never steady, never going head on.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” What is that person saying? He is taking accountability: I will bear the judgment of God, because I have sinned. “until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

Don’t try to get around the cause. Don’t try to deviate from the judgment. Don’t make excuses. Stop wavering. You asked God to show you, he has shown you where you are wrong, and now you are trying to bypass it: maybe I would be better if you brothers called me and checked in on me; it’s your fault. Do you think this is Disney and this is a ride? You can ride that pony by yourself.

Why will he bring me forth to the light? Because I don’t dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults and my errors because I want to get better, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging. We all fall short.

How do you endure in the truth? Listen, learn and live. There is no special recipe: when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. As soon as the medicine comes, people start running. The infraction does not tell who a person is so much as what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? If they can’t, they lose respect. All the big words mean nothing if, as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses because of pride and ego.

precepts.text: The nations shall lick the dust like a serpent, proving the cattle and beasts are the nations.
precepts.point: Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“The nations shall see and be confounded at all their might: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf. They shall lick the dust like a serpent, they shall move out of their holes like worms of the earth”. The nations lick the dust like a serpent.

That proves who the cattle and the beasts of the field are in the curse, “thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”: the cattle and the beasts are the nations. And licking the dust is the low estate of the serpent's curse, being made like a vagabond upon the earth, as Cain became a vagabond and Esau after him.

precepts.text: Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom; you cannot share everything on your mind even with the woman you lie down with.
precepts.point: This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says.
precepts.why:
Delilah “pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death”, and Samson “told her all his heart”. That is where he messed up. “Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.” You cannot share everything on your mind even with the woman you lie down with.

This is a scriptural example of why a man cannot tell his wife every single thing in his heart. We do not go by the philosophies of men that say your wife is your best friend you tell everything to; we do what the Bible says. Samson had kept the doors of his mouth three times; when he opened them, he gave away the secret of his strength.

precepts.text: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy; when I fall I shall arise, and when I sit in darkness the Lord shall be a light unto me. I will bear the indignation of the Lord because I have sinned, until he plead my cause; then she that is mine enemy shall see it and shame shall cover her, and she shall be trodden down as the mire of the streets. The Lord will fight on your behalf as long as you are doing what you must do.
precepts.point: Even his own familiar friend, in whom he trusted, who ate of his bread, has lifted up his heel against him. You have no clue who your real friends are until you fall.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“All that hate me whisper together against me: against me do they devise my hurt. An evil disease, say they, cleaveth fast unto him: and now that he lieth he shall rise up no more.” They rejoice in the affliction and disease David acquired through his transgressions. Micah answers that kind of enemy: “Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light unto me.”

“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me”. David owns his sin and bears the indignation, but the enemy who mocked it will see the outcome: “Then she that is mine enemy shall see it, and shame shall cover her which said unto me, Where is the Lord thy God? mine eyes shall behold her: now shall she be trodden down as the mire of the streets.” The Lord will fight on your behalf as long as you are doing what you must do.

This is a high level of hatred: “When shall he die, and his name perish?”, meaning when will this man be buried and just go. From other nations David is not surprised, but if you are in the truth and have this hatred toward your own people, that is wicked. When you fall in this truth, some spirits are built to mock and bring hurt to the spirit of the one who slipped, speaking vanity and flattering words to your face while the heart gathers iniquity, and slandering you abroad. Even his own familiar friend, in whom he trusted, who ate of his bread, lifted up his heel against him; you have no clue who your real friends are until you fall. But when I fall, I shall arise.

points: For the son dishonoureth the father, the daughter riseth up against her mother, the daughter in law against her mother in law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house. We have been watching that — the daughter rises up against the mother.
So brothers, you have to expect that when you repent, if your wife does not repent and your children do not repent, they will be the enemies in your house.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom. Do not be like Samson: he dealt with Delilah, and after a glorious time he just told her all his secrets. Do not counsel with your wife about stuff like that.

Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity? He retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy. Remember earlier we read that God does not change: if he had changed, all Israel would have been consumed.
Think about it, brothers: before you came here, some of the things you did were worthy of death. Why are you still alive? Because of God's mercy.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea. He is not going to remember them any more. We serve a merciful God.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide; keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom. Do not tell her everything; she will use what you say to destroy you. This is for you emotional brothers who think, I have to tell my wife everything. That is not what the scripture says.

A man's enemies are the men of his own house. You know your enemy; keep your friends close and your enemies closer, and you keep your eyes on them. But the woman sleeping in your bed, you are not keeping your eyes on her. Every time we talk about betrayal we look at the men, Judas Iscariot; but that same Judas spirit is in some of these sisters too. When you talk about agents being sent in among us, you always think about the men and never the women.

Article read in class: the story of Izola Ware Curry, the woman who nearly assassinated Martin Luther King Jr. A decade before his assassination, a black woman stabbed him with a letter opener at a Harlem book signing and nearly killed him. Most of you have never heard of her. Imagine if it had been a real knife. He did not expect that, from a black woman. You think Esau is going to walk in here or come to your house and stab you? I do not think so. Your enemy, brothers, is in your own house, eating your food, wearing your clothes, in your bed; those are the ones you are not paying attention to because you are too busy with other things.
The good man is perished out of the earth: and there is none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood; they hunt every man his brother with a net.
That they may do evil with both hands earnestly, the prince asketh, and the judge asketh for a reward; and the great man, he uttereth his mischievous desire: so they wrap it up.
Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.
For the son dishonoureth the father, the daughter riseth up against her mother, the daughter in law against her mother in law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.

note.label: Micah 7: He Will Subdue Our Iniquities

points: Therefore I will look unto the Lord; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me.
Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light unto me.

I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.
Then she that is mine enemy shall see it, and shame shall cover her which said unto me, Where is the Lord thy God?

note.label: Micah 7: He Will Subdue Our Iniquities

points: Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage; according to the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt will I shew unto him marvellous things.

The nations shall see and be confounded at all their might: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf. They shall lick the dust like a serpent, and shall be afraid of the Lord our God.
Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy.
He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, and the mercy to Abraham, which thou hast sworn unto our fathers from the days of old.
